signature: SUBROUTINE ZGEEV( JOBVL, JOBVR, N, A, LDA, W, VL, LDVL, VR, LDVR,

params.name: jobvl
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: left eigenvectors of A are not computed;
-   `= 'V'`: left eigenvectors of are computed.

params.name: jobvr
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: right eigenvectors of A are not computed;
-   `= 'V'`: right eigenvectors of A are computed.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, A has been overwritten.
params.workDependent: the Schur form T follows the eigenvalue order, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change, and is unique only up to unit phases

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: w
params.workDependent: the order in which the eigenvalues deflate depends on the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking

params.name: VL
params.reference: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `JOBVL = 'N'`, `VL` is not referenced. $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VL`.
params.workDependent: the eigenvector columns follow the eigenvalue order, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change

params.name: ldvl
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array `VL`. $\mathrm{LDVL} \ge 1$; if `JOBVL = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LDVL} \ge N$.

params.name: VR
params.reference: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `JOBVR = 'N'`, `VR` is not referenced. $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VR`.
params.workDependent: the eigenvector columns follow the eigenvalue order, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change

params.name: ldvr
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array `VR`. $\mathrm{LDVR} \ge 1$; if `JOBVR = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LDVR} \ge N$.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,2 \, N)$. For good performance, `LWORK` must generally be larger.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, the QR algorithm failed to compute all the eigenvalues, and no eigenvectors have been computed; elements i+1:N of W contain eigenvalues which have converged.

untranslated: WORK.minLength: local MINWRK is assigned inside nested control flow

overrides.reason: ZGEEV hands its LWORK to ZGEHRD, ZUNGHR, ZHSEQR and ZTREVC3, which pick their block size, AED window or back-transformation from LWORK. The blocked and unblocked Hessenberg reductions round differently, and the QR iteration that follows can then deflate the eigenvalues in another order, so W, the Schur form T in A (also unique only up to unit phases), and the eigenvector columns that follow W's order all change. The reference does this as well: compiled LAPACK 3.12.0 ZGEEV (random matrix, JOBVR = 'V') returns a different A and a different order of W at LWORK = 2N than at its optimum for N = 150, 200 and 300. The JS zgehrd crosses over at NX = 32 where ILAENV(3) gives 128, so the JS path changes from N > 33 (the reference's from N > 128): at N = 80 and 120 the JS result at WORK = 2N is bit-identical to the one with only zgehrd held unblocked, and matches the optimum's spectrum to 5e-14 with 4 and 18 eigenvalues reordered and the matched eigenvectors equal to 2e-14. The module's tests check the spectrum and the eigenvector residuals at the minimum WORK past the blocking threshold (ticket 0100).

set.params.VR.workDependent: the eigenvector columns follow the eigenvalue order, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change
